title: Blue being trained as police dog in Alberta
article: The grandson of slain police dog, Cyr, is set to fill the role left by the tragic death of his relative as the new partner of Cst. Steve Kaye.
Blue, a 14-month-old German shepherd, will be received by Kaye this morning in Sherwood Park, Alberta, then trained to become Kaye's new canine colleague.

Kaye, was unavailable for comment Tuesday but Bill Hargarten, superintendent of the police K-9 unit, said Kaye talked to him earlier in the day and described Blue as "a clone of Cyr with tremendous potential to succeed as a police dog."

Cyr had placed among the top five dogs at the Canadian Police Canine Championships in both 1999 and 2000. Blue will go through strict training over the next few months to see if he has the qualifications to become a K-9 member.
Despite the gain, it will be some time before Kaye and his family no longer feel so heavyhearted about the death of their partner and pet.
"I don't think it will ease the loss of Cyr anytime soon. It hasn't been easy on anyone," said Kaye's wife Corinne.
Cyr, a five-year-old German shepherd, was shot during a brief armed standoff east of the city on May 20.
The dog was shot by a suspect who had led city police and RCMP on a chase before threatening them with a gun. The suspect, Keldon McMillan, was later shot by police and died at the scene.
Like all police dogs, Cyr lived with his handler and was essentially a family pet during his off-duty hours. Police dogs accompany their handlers throughout every 12-hour shift.
The death of Cyr also fell hard on Peg O'Neil, who raised him and trained him with early skills as a pup.
"It was quite hard for us to hear about it," said O'Neil, who runs Heartridge Training Academy in Sherwood Park, which supplies police dogs to many forces in Canada.

"It will be mixed feelings dealing with the loss of Cyr and having a new dog, but ultimately, Blue has a lot of the same characteristics that Cyr had and that is what will probably do a lot of healing for those who were impacted (by the death)."
